utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-95-5/18-T, The Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I have the appearances, from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone. For the Prosecution, Mr. Alan Tieger, myself, Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff, and we are accompanied by Ms. Angelique Langenberg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies. I'm here on behalf of my Defence together with my senior advisor, Mr. Peter Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber has decided to hold this Status Conference upon the request of the accused. Before we begin, I would like to provide a short background to this Status Conference. On the 28th of January, 2015, the Chamber held a Status Conference upon the request of the accused where the accused could raise any specific concern as to his health and the conditions of his detention. On the 12th of May, 2015, the Chamber denied the accused's new request to convene another Status Conference as it considered that the accused had not identified any specific remedy he sought from the Chamber. The Chamber stated that it would not entertain of a general nature that do not relate to the accused personally and that there was no disclosure-related matter that warranted the holding of a Status Conference. On the 24th of August, the Chamber was informed via e-mail from the accused's legal advisor that the accused was suffering from a number of symptoms. Not having been informed of his medical condition or state of health, the Chamber requested that the Registry file a medical report. The medical report was filed confidentially on the 28th of August, and the Chamber was informed that the accused had undergone surgery. Upon the request of the accused, the Chamber ordered the reclassification of the medical report as public. On the 1st of September, the accused asked the Chamber to hold a Status Conference to discuss health, conditions of detention and continuing disclosure violations by the Office of the Prosecutor. On the 16th of September, the Chamber issued an interim order, stating that the issue of disclosure had highly been litigated in writing, and, therefore, there was no specific issue not addressed in writing which warranted holding a Status Conference, and that the Chamber would not entertain concerns of a general nature which did not pertain to the accused. However, in relation to the accused's health and conditions of detention, the Chamber ordered that the accused file a supplemental submission, identifying the specific issues to be discussed and the remedies sought. On the 18th of September, the accused filed his additional submission; and on 22nd of September, the Chamber decided to hold a Status Conference so that the accused could raise specific issues related to his health and conditions of detention as listed in his supplemental submission. That said, now, Mr. Karadzic, you have the floor on the specific issues in relation to your health and conditions of detention.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. As per the items contained in my request, first, I wanted to touch upon some events in August. But, first, I wanted to say that I arrived here in an exemplary health, or health condition, which was the result of a very strict regimen I applied in how I lived my life as well as the application of some aspects of eastern medicine. My laboratory findings were perfect. At the very outset I noticed that some things will be a hindrance here, and I had an extensive correspondence with the management of the Detention Unit as well as the medical service there. It was clear to me straight away that certain things will cause a disbalance in my health status because I could no longer use certain supplements I relied on before my arrival here. The most serious concern for all in the UNDU is food which remains of poor quality and different, or strange, taste when it comes to people from the Balkans. The food served is mostly frozen and warmed up in a microwave immediately prior to being served, which is detrimental, highly detrimental. As for any other food items, such as dairy products that we receive once a day for breakfast or dinner, that is quite acceptable and we try to preserve it as long as we can, depending on the circumstances. If the UN wing is the same as the rest of the prison, it is my belief that young offenders who are in full health can consume such food without any consequences, but our Detention Unit resembles a nursing home rather than a youth centre for young delinquents. We are mostly intellectuals, and no one there is under 50 or 55. Most of us are over 60; some are older than 70. We come from a completely different culture, and seldom can they adjust to new taste of that kind. We usually do not eat our meals in full, and I had my -- I can forward my entire correspondence that I had with the Detention Unit to the Chamber, if needed. The main problem is the storage of food. Those of us who work late into the night after 8.30 p.m., no longer have any access to the common room or the kitchen facilities, and yet we need food, keeping it in our cells. There, we don't have any refrigeration units. As far as I know, in some other buildings of the complex it is possible to rent a small fridge which would be of much assistance. I ended up asking for a passive cool box which does not need a source of power. Dr. Falke was in favour of that, but I have still not received it. I am in particularly difficult circumstances because I mostly worked on my Defence during the night, and it is my habit. The crisis that occurred in August was a result of all those things. Before that, I had eight of my teeth broken or chipped, for example, while eating a banana. It is a very clear indicator that there is something wrong with the metabolism and something missing. I was in contact with the management and the medical service in 2010. I still have that correspondence, advising them of my so-called metabolic syndrome as I call it. I see it as the beginning of the worsening of my physical health and I tried to counter it with the means available. However, I was unable to. At the outset, the nurses were very kind and brought food which they had purchased outside the prison in terms of what I needed. I made use of those useful supplements but after a while, it was forbidden to them to do so, and I could no longer obtain them. I was informed that many other detainees suffer from similar problems and that some of them developed some very serious conditions or their existing conditions worsened. Because of the teeth problems, I had to use analgesic painkillers, which damaged my digestion; first and foremost my stomach. The entire second half of August was marked by strong gastritis incidents, which, for a while, hindered the diagnosis of the gall condition, turning out that there was a large gall-bladder in my body. Owing to your intervention, which I would like to thank you for, I was you are subsequently examined. I was sent for an ultrasound check the very same day, and they realised that the gall condition was critical. There was a danger of it bursting causing further complications similar to the ones suffered here by a general in the Detention Unit. Had the gall burst, the very next day I would have turned yellow and my condition would have suffered. I was sent for examination the very same day and hospitalised. I received infusion and prepared for an operation. The operation followed. (redacted) (redacted) My convalescence went well but in terms of my metabolism and other issues, they still remain. Several detainees developed diabetes while being there, or their pre-existing diagnosis worsened. I believe it is not possible to cure or pre-empt the development of a disease in conditions that cause it. If there are so many incidences of diabetes one must give thought to the environment or else it is useless unless conditions are changed. It is difficult to expect any change in the situation overall if we do not tackle that. My glucosis level has been stabilized in the meantime through the application of oral therapy. Given the fact that it occurred only a year or two ago, since my arrival here, it seems that my blood vessels remain intact despite the symptoms. However, unless I'm treated, that situation will not persist. In terms of diabetes, there are some long and short-term problems. Short-term problems are lack of concentration and poor memory because my cells are unable to use adequate sugar levels. Long-term consequences are the damage to the blood vessels and some organs. The use of glucosis in the brain and the muscles is made impossible unless there are sufficient levels of insulin. Since the time when I had the correspondence about the conditions in my health, events developed catastrophically. I have in mind item D, which provides me with an opportunity to address you on the issues that need to be resolved. There are no guarantees whatsoever that should events continue, I will not be affected. The events in question are as follows. There were two sudden deaths and two suicides that took place in the Detention Unit before my arrival. Just before my arrival and since that time, the following happened: Eleven detainees were diagnosed with serious malignant diseases some of them are no longer with us because the diagnosis came too late for treatment. Such a high rate of incidents in such a small sample requires full attention, first and foremost by the UN because we are their responsibility. It also calls for an investigation by the World Health Organisation. There was another suicide after the person in question had served their sentence. There was a serious case of physical disability resulting in an interruption in the trial. Another eight detainees developed serious diseases or saw their existing diseases worsen. What we probably receive in the Detention Unit is customary for the legal and custodial system of the Netherlands, but as it turns out, with people who are fragile and growing old, it is no longer sufficient. We need to examine whether it is the issue of food, the construction material used in the Detention Unit, or something else. We should give thought to some changes in the medical coverage system so as to have a doctor present every day. I cannot explain about specific people. The staff are very fair and everything is fine, but the system is flawed because it resulted in the sequence of events. God forbid hopefully there will be no longer malignant diseases occurring, there are no conditions to the contrary. The incidence is so high that I am surprised that no one is doing anything about it. I wrote to the UN DU management asking that they should require an investigation and no one did anything. There must be a certain factor in the environment there which causes all this. This was by way of an introduction. If you would like to have any further clarification, I am at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me draw your attention to page 7, line -- there's mention of a physical disability but I was talking about psychological mental state, state of psychosis which caused the interruption in the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is relieved to hear that you are personally well at the moment, recovering from the surgery. The Chamber has duly noted your observation as to the general condition of detention at the Detention Unit but I believe there is a regime which I believe is fully functioning, but since you are seeking no specific remedy, I will repeat what we said in our previous order, that the Chamber gives the highest regard to your health. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there's no need for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Judge Morrison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, are you able to get sufficient physical exercise?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. Now I do, because I don't have to work on preparations anymore, and now I get more physical exercise. I go walking, I play tennis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I asked that because, although I may be wrong, my impression is that you lost a bit of weight since I last saw you face to face, but that may be as a result of an exercise regime as much as anything else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, the passive cool box that you requested, was it refused or is it in the pipeline? Any idea at all?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A year ago, Dr. Falke said that that should be approved. I wrote them, but it still didn't happen. These people are excellent but rules are absolutely senseless. It's absolutely senseless, some of these things. For instance, there are people who are vegetarians or people who observe the Orthodox lent and they have no fridges to keep this food. It was not enough for Dr. Falke to say that it should be approved, that it's reasonable. There's a good reason. I absolutely can't see why cool boxes can't be kept. It would be good for our health. At least that passive cool box. Apart from that, the food the ICC prisoners get is much better because they simply refused to some other things, and they got something better. But the United Nations is overseeing both courts. I don't see any point in this. I'm not actually asking for them to be deprived of it, I'm asking for the same thing to be given to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, what Judge Kwon said is not what I'm asking. I am asking for an inquiry to be made and to exclude the possibility of this malignancy on rampage, because it's very unusual that the incidence of disease be so high on such a small sample of population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, what you have raised does not seem to be within the competence of the Trial Chamber. There are proper ways through which you can raise those issues vis-à-vis the Detention Unit and the Registrar; also as to the monitoring and supervision of the Detention Unit, I also believe there is a proper regime separately. Unless there's another matter to be raised -- yes. Judge Morrison has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, it's a request more than a question, Dr. Karadzic. We didn't find out about your gall-bladder problems until pretty late in the day or the events that preceded them. So what we would simply ask is that if your health starts to deteriorate in the future that we are informed as soon as practicable at as early a stage as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I always gave approval for the Trial Chamber to be kept informed, but so far, before disturbing the Trial Chamber I wrote letters through all the proper channels, and if the Trial Chamber is interested, I could make it available to them, for the Chamber to see that before addressing the Chamber, I did address all the proper instances. But the rules are probably designed for another type of population, not this one, so I was not successful in getting the attention of these other instances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Now the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: at 9.31 a.m.
